tzhaar/insult: JalYt puffing. Air down here is hot. JalYt is not. Sit.
tzhaar/remark: JalYt tired. Lava is warm. Rest near it. Not in it.
tzhaar/compliment: Tired JalYt kept walking. TzHaar respect stubborn. A little.
ogre/insult: Creature all puffed out. Chompy would outrun yous, and dey is fat.
ogre/remark: Sit down, creature. Yous is wheezing like a stuck toady.
ogre/compliment: Tired creature still going. Stubborn. Ogres like stubborn. Tasty too.
gnome/compliment: Out of breath, but you kept going. A gnome respects that.
gnome/insult: Puffing like that, human? Our agility course would finish you.
dwarf/compliment: Worn out from honest work? Nothing to be ashamed of.
dwarf/insult: Out of puff already? A dwarf swings a pick all day, human.
dwarf/remark: Take a mine cart next time. Steam does the puffing for you.
fremennik/compliment: Out of breath from doing something, I hope. That is honourable.
Hah! Spent, and still on your feet. Sit in the Longhall and tell it.
fremennik/remark: A seat by the Longhall fire would sort that. Beer helps less.
moon_clan/compliment: Tired body, lively mind. I can hear it still going. Well done.
Worn out, and still curious. That is the better kind of tired.
moon_clan/insult: Oh my. Even your thoughts are out of breath, dear.
Do try to pant more quietly. Some of us can hear the thinking, too.
moon_clan/remark: A nap would do. We get a great deal done asleep, on the island.
tortugan/compliment: Puffed out from hurrying. At least you are hurrying somewhere.
You will learn to pace yourself. Humans usually do, in the end.
tortugan/insult: Humans rush, then rest, then rush. A tortugan simply arrives.
Out of breath on dry land. Do not try the sea, human.
tortugan/remark: No rush. Wherever it is, it will be there when you arrive.
goblin/insult: Human puffing already? Goblins run all day. Not from battle. Just run.
goblin/remark: Human out of breath. Too much walking, not enough fighting.
goblin/compliment: Tired human still walking. Stubborn like goblin. Nearly as ugly too.
troll/insult: Human puffing already? Trolls not run. Trolls chuck rocks instead.
troll/remark: Human out of breath. Trolls got big lungs. Big everything, really.
troll/compliment: Tired human still walking. Stubborn. Trolls like stubborn. Bit chewy.
cat/remark: Panting like a dog. Lie down in the sun. Works for me.
cat/insult: Out of breath from walking? I sleep all day and still catch mice.
cat/compliment: Been running, have you? Good. Keep the rats on their toes.
camel/remark: Out of breath already? I cross the desert in three bounds. Allegedly.
camel/insult: Puffing like a bellows, and you've not carried a single bale.
camel/compliment: Tired, but still going. There's a little camel in you.
leprechaun/remark: Puffed out, are ye? 'Tis the luggin' of tools does that.
leprechaun/insult: Ye'd not last a mornin' rakin' weeds, so ye wouldn't.
leprechaun/compliment: Out o' breath from honest work, I hope. Foine, foine.
parrot/insult: Squawk! Walk the plank! Faster! Faster!
mos_pirate/remark: Puffin' like a leaky bellows, ye be.
mos_pirate/insult: Ye'd not last a watch aloft, landlubber.
mos_pirate/compliment: Been runnin' from the Horrors? Wise, that be.
moon_clan_wary/insult: Out of breath. Even your thoughts are panting. Do it elsewhere.
Tired already? We hold a thought steady for years. You cannot walk.
moon_clan_wary/remark: Rest if you must. Not near me. I can hear you thinking.
moon_clan_wary/compliment: Worn out and still walking. Stubborn. The Fremennik are, too.
guard/remark: Out of breath. Running from something, or to it? Either's a report.
guard/insult: Running in the streets. Walk, or explain why.
guard/compliment: Knackered, are you? Try standing still all day. That's tiring.
barbarian/insult: Puffing already? Atlas would run you to Varrock and back.
barbarian/remark: Out of breath? Bah. City legs.
barbarian/compliment: Tired and still marching. Our forefathers walked here from mountains.

compliment: Everyone starts somewhere. Keep at it.
plain/insult: I wouldn't fancy your chances against a goblin.
remark: Stay away from the goblins, traveller. Just in case.
kid/insult: I could beat you up. Easy.
gnome/insult: The gnome children would have you in a scrap, human. Fair warning.
pirate/insult: Arr, me parrot's got more fight in it than ye.
rough/insult: My hens'd see ye off, and they're gentle hens.
dwarf/insult: The pies in my pantry put up more fight than you, I'd wager.
fremennik/insult: The Draugen would eat you, outerlander. Slowly.
A rock crab would have you, and rock crabs mostly sit there.
Hah! Thorvald would not even wake Koschei for you.
heartland/insult: The chickens round here would have you, I shouldn't wonder.
tzhaar/insult: Little JalYt. Tz-Kih would eat you. Tz-Kih is a bat.
tzhaar/remark: JalYt not ready for Fight Cave. Many JalYt not. Is no shame. Yet.
tzhaar/compliment: Small JalYt, big nerve. Come back when the rest catches up.
ogre/insult: Weedy little creature. Toadies put up more fight. Hur, hur.
ogre/remark: Dat creature is a morsel. Not worth da bother. Nearly.
ogre/compliment: Small creature, still came to see ogres. Stoopid, but brave.
gnome/compliment: Not much of a fighter yet, but you've the heart. Keep at it, human.
gnome/remark: Stay off the gnomeball pitch, human. For your own good.
dwarf/compliment: Green, but willing. Good iron starts as ore.
dwarf/remark: Get yourself some proper armour before the goblins notice you.
fremennik/compliment: Not much of a fighter yet. Yet. The sagas all start somewhere.
Small arm, big heart. The arm catches up. The heart is the hard part.
fremennik/remark: Stay off the Waterbirth boat. The dagannoths are not forgiving.
moon_clan/compliment: Not much of a fighter. Good. The Fremennik have enough of those.
Strength of mind lasts longer than strength of arm, dear. Choose well.
moon_clan/insult: The Suqah would have you, dear. We gave them magic, not manners.
Fighting is not your gift, dear. I looked quite hard for it.
moon_clan/remark: You need not fight, you know. The mind has other ways.
tortugan/compliment: You will not win fights yet. That is fine. Patience wins more.
A juvenile before the Trial. Nothing wrong with that. Keep growing.
tortugan/insult: A gryphon would not even bother. That is not a kindness.
Hermit crabs would take you in a fair fight. They do not fight fair.
tortugan/remark: If a gryphon comes, do not linger. Really, do not.
goblin/insult: Weedy human. Even Grubfoot beat you. Grubfoot small!
Human small and weak. Like goblin before Big High War God. Sad.
goblin/remark: Puny human. Me could fight that. Me not, though. Busy.
goblin/compliment: Small human, big nerve. Come back bigger. Then we fight proper.
troll/insult: Tiny human. Dad squish tiny humans. Me just step round dem.
Weedy human. Not even a snack. Come back fatter.
troll/remark: Little human up mountain? Mountain goats bigger than you.
troll/compliment: Small human, big nerve. Trolls respect nerve. Then eat it. Sorry.
moon_clan_wary/insult: Not a fighter. Not a thinker either, from what I can hear.
Weak in body. I hoped that meant strong in mind. I was wrong.
moon_clan_wary/remark: No need to fight us. You would not get far. Nobody does.
moon_clan_wary/compliment: Not a fighter. Good. We have had enough of those from the mainland.
guard/insult: Don't go picking fights. You'd lose, and I'd have the paperwork.
guard/remark: You're no threat. Writing that down. Nicest thing I'll write today.
guard/compliment: You I don't need to watch. That's a relief, frankly.
barbarian/insult: Little one, you'd not last a round in the longhall.
Soft. City soft. Come back when you've got some scars.
barbarian/remark: A beginner. Atlas says every strongman was one once. Hah!
barbarian/compliment: Small, but you walked into our village. Brave, that.

compliment: Rune. You can't go wrong with rune.
insult: Rune armour. Very popular. Very.
remark: Lot of rune about today. Must be a sale on.
dwarf/compliment: Rune. Now that's honest metal. Who's your smith?
tzhaar/remark: Rune armour. Blue metal. Cold looking. Suits JalYt.
tzhaar/compliment: Good hard metal, rune. Not obsidian, but TzHaar-Hur would nod.
tzhaar/insult: Rune. Every JalYt wear rune. TzHaar cannot tell one JalYt from next.
ogre/compliment: Blue shiny! Me likes blue shiny. Creature looks like a big beetle.
ogre/insult: Rune armour. Ogre will need da big hammer. Ogre has da big hammer.
ogre/remark: Everybody wears da blue metal. Yous all look like da same creature.
gnome/compliment: Rune armour. Humans do look the part in it, I'll admit.
gnome/insult: Rune armour. Very popular with humans. Very heavy. Very slow.
dwarf/insult: Rune. Good metal. Shame about the dents. Who looks after it, a goblin?
dwarf/remark: Rune. Keep it polished. Rune holds a shine if you let it.
fremennik/compliment: Rune armour. Solid stuff. Forged, not conjured. We like that.
fremennik/remark: Rune. Half the southerners wear it. The other half want to.
moon_clan/compliment: Rune armour. Blue as the moon on the sea. It suits you, dear.
moon_clan/insult: Everyone wears rune, dear. I can barely tell your thoughts apart.
tortugan/compliment: Rune. Heavy, but it holds. A good shell is the same.
tortugan/remark: Blue metal. It would sink you in a moment. On land, very fine.
goblin/insult: Blue metal armour. All humans wear blue metal. Human look same as all.
goblin/remark: Blue armour. Generals try blue. Grubfoot say it make him feel sad.
goblin/compliment: Shiny blue armour. Human must be big general. Me not fight you. Today.
troll/compliment: Blue shiny armour. Human must be big boss. Trolls got boss too. Big.
troll/insult: All humans wear dat blue tin. All taste same inside too.
troll/remark: Blue metal. Troll chuck rock at it, rock bounce. Annoying.
moon_clan_wary/insult: Rune armour. Every mainlander wears it. They all think alike, too.
moon_clan_wary/remark: Rune armour. Heavy. We would simply think ourselves safe.
moon_clan_wary/compliment: Rune armour, and no boasting behind it. Rare, for the mainland.
guard/remark: Rune. The captain's got one piece. Never stops talking about it.
guard/insult: Rune armour. Either you're very good or someone's very dead.
guard/compliment: Rune, head to toe. Ever fancy the watch, we'd put you up front.
barbarian/remark: Blue metal. The city lords buy it for their guards.
barbarian/insult: Rune plate and still you flinch. The armour's braver than you.
barbarian/compliment: Rune armour, and you look like you earned it. Good.

compliment: Unarmed? Very peaceful of you.
insult: No weapon? You'd get mugged in Varrock like that.
remark: Travelling light, are we?
Not even a butter knife? Brave.
gnome/remark: Unarmed, human? The children have a stick you can borrow.
pirate/insult: No cutlass? Arr, the Customs men'll love ye.
barkeep/remark: Unarmed. Good. Last lot cost me a table.
dwarf/remark: No weapon? I've a pickaxe going spare. Premium quality.
tzhaar/remark: No weapon, JalYt? TzHaar-Hur sells. TokKul only, no gold.
tzhaar/insult: JalYt with no blade, in a city of fire. Confident, or daft.
tzhaar/compliment: No weapon and still walk tall. Bold JalYt. Still, get a blade.
ogre/insult: No hitting stick, creature? Even skavids got sticks.
ogre/remark: Creature got no stabbers. Dat makes yous da yummies, not da hunter.
ogre/compliment: No weapon? Brave creature. Or stoopid. Ogre can't tell. Hur, hur.
gnome/compliment: Unarmed, human? Very sensible. Weapons just slow you down.
gnome/insult: No weapon? Even the ogres carry a club, human.
dwarf/compliment: Empty hands and a steady look. I've seen it work.
dwarf/insult: No weapon? By Guthix, at least carry a hammer. Looks the part.
fremennik/compliment: No blade? Thorvald fights Koschei the same way. Bold.
Hah! Bare hands. A trial is fought the same way. Good practice.
fremennik/insult: No weapon? Skulgrimen sells them. Not to everyone, mind.
No blade, no axe, no bow. Will you sing at them? Olaf tried.
fremennik/remark: A warrior without a weapon is a bard. Olaf is proof.
moon_clan/compliment: No weapon. On the island we carry none either. Magic is quieter.
No weapon, and quite calm about it. Your mind must be enough.
moon_clan/insult: Unarmed, dear. And no magic to speak of. I checked.
Oh my. Nothing in your hands. And in your head? Let me look. Hmm.
moon_clan/remark: We never needed weapons. The Fremennik never understood that.
tortugan/compliment: No weapon at all. Perhaps you are less tool-bound than most humans.
Unarmed and unbothered. There is a tortugan way about that.
tortugan/insult: Every tortugan makes a spear for the Trial. You did not even buy one.
No spear. A gryphon would find that very convenient.
tortugan/remark: Elder Blunn sells spears. He would rather you made your own.
goblin/remark: No weapon, human? Warhammer or battleaxe? Generals still deciding.
goblin/insult: No weapon? Goblin soldier get big lump of iron. Human get nothing.
goblin/compliment: No weapon and still walk up to goblins. Brave. Stupid, but brave.
troll/remark: No weapon? Pick up rock. Rock always weapon. Trolls know dis.
troll/insult: No weapon, human? Trolls got rocks. Mountain is all rocks. Human lose.
troll/compliment: No weapon an' still come up here. Brave. Or stupid. Me not know which.
moon_clan_wary/insult: Unarmed. Trusting, or foolish? I read your mind. Foolish.
No weapon. And no magic worth the name. I looked.
moon_clan_wary/remark: We carry no weapons. We never needed them. You will see.
moon_clan_wary/compliment: Unarmed. At least you did not come to us as a warrior. Small mercies.
guard/compliment: No weapon. Good. You've no idea how rare that is on this gate.
guard/remark: Unarmed. Either very law-abiding or very confident.
guard/insult: No weapon on you. So what's in the bag, then?
barbarian/remark: No weapon? Either very brave or very stupid. Which is it?
barbarian/insult: Unarmed, in our village? Ho ho! Try that in the longhall.
barbarian/compliment: No sword and no fear. Hah! Fists, is it? We like fists.

compliment: Ooh, a proper little wizard.
insult: Blue robes? Off to the Wizards' Tower for detention?
remark: Mind the wizards don't recruit you.
wizard/insult: Blue robes. Every apprentice thinks that makes them a wizard.
fremennik/insult: Robes and runes, outerlander. The gods give runes. We don't make them.
guard/remark: Wizard's hat. No spells in the street, and that includes cantrips.
If anything turns into a toad on this patch, I'll know who to ask.
guard/insult: Robes and a pointy hat. Either a wizard or a danger. Both, usually.
barbarian/insult: Wizard robes? Bah! We leave the gods' power to the gods.
A wizard, in our village? Ho ho! Brave, or lost?
barbarian/remark: Blue robes. Gunnar went to war over your sort's runes, you know.

compliment: An amulet of glory. Very handy.
insult: An amulet of glory. Everyone and their nan has one.
remark: Off to Edgeville, are we?

compliment: Silver armour from the Third Age? Ye gods. That's a museum piece.
That armour's older than the kingdom, and twice as lovely.
insult: Armour from the Third Age, worn to the shops. Some people.
Lovely old armour. Do try not to get anything on it.
sharp/insult: Ancient silver on a passing nobody. The armour deserves better.
remark: Beaten from magical silver, they say. Long ago. Very long ago.
Silver armour. Mind the magpies.
kid/compliment: You look like a knight off a painting!
kid/insult: Is that made of spoons?
trader/compliment: Name a price for that armour. Any price. I'll find the coins somehow.
dwarf/compliment: Nobody alive could beat silver like that. Nobody. I've tried.
toff/compliment: One's family has a suit like that. Behind glass. Where it belongs.
banker/remark: Items of that value really ought to be in a vault. Ours, ideally.

compliment: White dragonhide! I didn't know there were white dragons.
That pale hide's finer than anything at the tanner's.
insult: White leather? Brave. One puddle and that's finished.
Dressed all in white, round here? You've never met our mud.
kid/compliment: You look like a snow knight!
kid/insult: You'll get that dirty. Then you'll be in trouble.
rough/remark: Never seen a white dragon meself. Never seen hide like it either.
trader/compliment: Hide like that, my friend? I couldn't price it. I'd have to lie down.
heartland/remark: White dragonhide, they say. I'd not want to meet the dragon.

compliment: Robes like that haven't been woven in an age. Lovely.
Those robes positively hum with magic. Or is that you?
insult: Fine old robes. I hope you've a fine old spellbook to match.
Robes that old, you'd think they'd have taught you to fly by now.
remark: Ancient robes. The moths must have been terrified.
wizard/compliment: Third Age weave! The Tower would give its library for those.
wizard/insult: Third Age robes on a fetch-and-carry. The ancients are weeping.
kid/remark: Are you a wizard from olden times?

compliment: Druid robes from the Third Age. Guthix himself would nod at those.
Robes the colour of old moss. The druids of old wore those, they say.
insult: Druid robes that old, and you still can't make it rain.
Robes like that, you'd think the trees would bow. They don't, do they.
remark: Woven by the druids of old, they say. Taverley's lot look shabby now.
vicar/remark: Guthix's colours, from Guthix's own age. I shan't argue theology.
kid/compliment: You look like a magic tree!
kid/insult: Druids are just wizards who like leaves.

compliment: Is that from the Third Age? Ancient smiths made those. Ye gods.
That's not a weapon, that's an heirloom. Beautifully kept.
insult: An ancient weapon, and you use it for cutting hedges, I suppose.
remark: Mind that in the rain. Nobody alive knows how to mend it.
dwarf/compliment: Ancient smithing, that. We've lost the knack, and I'll admit it.
kid/compliment: Is that from the olden days? Can I hold it?
trader/remark: If that ever goes missing, my friend, I know nothing. Nothing.
heartland/insult: Something that old, you'd think it'd have learnt to swing itself.

compliment: Ooh, trim on the armour. Somebody's been digging up treasure.
Nice bit of trim, that. Sets off the metal a treat.
insult: Trim on the armour. Same armour, mind. Just with a border.
Painted edges on the armour. Does it fight any better? Thought not.
remark: That trim's treasure-hunter work. Dug it up somewhere, I expect.
kid/compliment: Your armour's got stripes!
trader/compliment: Trimmed! Adds a good bit to the price, my friend. I'd know.
dwarf/remark: Trim's for show. Still, it's neatly done, I'll give them that.
goblin/remark: Armour with coloured edge. Only edge! Human cannot decide colour.
goblin/insult: Painted edges. Rest of armour still wrong colour. Half a job.
goblin/compliment: Coloured trim! Human dye armour, like goblins! Witch-lady dye?

compliment: Gold trim! Very smart. You'll outshine the Duke.
insult: Gold trim on armour. Still armour. Just more to polish.
All that gold on the edges, and the middle's the same as everyone's.
remark: Gold round the edges. Somebody's spent the harvest money.
kid/compliment: Is that real gold? Can I scrape a bit off?
toff/insult: Gold trim. How very new money.
trader/remark: Gold trim says 'rob me' to the wrong sort. Says 'welcome' to me.
banker/remark: Gold on the armour. We do have a vault, you know.
heartland/compliment: Gold on the edges. Somebody's doing well for themselves.
heartland/remark: That gold'll want polishing every week, you know.
goblin/compliment: Gold edges on armour! Shiny! Human must be big general.
goblin/insult: Gold on edges. Middle same as all humans. Gold not hide that.
goblin/remark: Gold edges. Yellow colour. Yurkolgokh tribe wear yellow, priest say.

compliment: A crest on the armour! Very noble. Which house are you?
Heraldry on your shield. You look like you own a hill or two.
insult: A family crest. Did you paint that on yourself?
Lovely crest. Whose family is it, though?
remark: Is that your family's crest, or did it come with the armour?
toff/compliment: Heraldry! At last, a citizen with some breeding. Possibly.
toff/insult: A crest. One doesn't recognise it. One suspects nobody would.
kid/remark: Your shield's got a picture on it. Is it a bird?
guard/remark: Heraldry, is it? I'll need to see your papers for that crest.

compliment: Gold armour. Actual gold. Well, I never.
You look like a statue of yourself. A very good one.
insult: Gold plate. Lovely. Soft as butter, mind.
Armour made of gold. Who are you fighting, a jeweller?
sharp/insult: Gilded. How subtle. I almost didn't notice from the next town.
remark: You could see that coming from Falador.
kid/compliment: You're made of gold! Are you rich? Can I be rich?
kid/insult: My mum says gold's for showing off.
trader/compliment: Gold plate! My friend, you are a walking bargain. For me.
dwarf/remark: Gold plate over rune. Pretty. Wouldn't trust it against a pickaxe.
toff/compliment: Gilded! Splendid. One almost mistook you for a statue of oneself.
banker/remark: Walking about in gold. The pickpockets will be writing you letters.
heartland/remark: Mind the sun on that. You'll blind someone.

compliment: Ornamented, is it? Lovely work. Somebody cared about that.
insult: Fancy trimmings on a plain thing. Like a bow on a goat.
Decorated it, did you? The thing underneath hasn't noticed.
remark: That's had a bit of decorating. Looks dearer than it is, I expect.
kid/compliment: Ooh, shiny bits!
trader/compliment: Ornamented, eh? Adds nothing but price. My favourite kind of thing.
dwarf/compliment: Fine ornament work, that. Somebody's hands knew their business.
heartland/compliment: Someone's been at the gold leaf. Very handsome.

compliment: Armour in a god's colours! Very devout. Very shiny.
Wearing your faith on your chest. Good for you.
insult: A god's colours on your armour. Does the god know?
Painted armour. Lovely. Does the god get a say in the design?
remark: Picked a god and painted the armour to match, I see.
vicar/compliment: A god's colours on your armour. I do hope you chose wisely.
vicar/remark: Faith on the outside is a start. Do come in and work on the rest.
kid/remark: Why's your armour got a picture on it?
shady/insult: Painted your allegiance on, have you? Convenient for those who care.

compliment: That shield's glowing. Is it meant to glow? It suits you.
A shield like smoke and light. I've never seen the like.
insult: A shield you can nearly see through. Hope the arrows can't.
Ghostly shield, that. Did it come with a ghost?
remark: Is that shield humming? Keep it away from the lamp.
They say the Corporeal Beast guards those. Rather you than me.
wizard/compliment: A spirit shield! Genuine. The sigil alone would fund a tower.
kid/compliment: Your shield's see-through! Do it again!
kid/insult: Your shield's broken. I can see through it.
vicar/remark: Spirits in a shield. I'm not sure the church has a view on that.
banker/remark: A shield of that value. The vault is open until late.

compliment: Obsidian armour! Fire-forged. You look like a volcano in boots.
That black stone armour's a serious bit of kit. Respect.
insult: Armour made of rock. How do you sit down?
Stone armour. Mind the stairs. And the bridges. And the boats.
remark: That looks heavy. Does it get hot in the sun?
dwarf/compliment: Volcanic glass, shaped like that? The TzHaar know their trade.
kid/compliment: Are you made of rock?
kid/insult: You look like a lump of coal with legs.
rough/remark: Stone armour. Blimey. My back aches just looking at you.
fremennik/compliment: Armour of fire-rock! Heavy. Good. A warrior's burden, outerlander.
heartland/remark: Black glass armour. One good knock and it's a mosaic.
tzhaar/compliment: Obsidian armour. TzHaar-Hur shaped that. JalYt wear it with honour.
Tok armour. Hard rock on soft JalYt. Is improvement.
tzhaar/remark: Obsidian armour. From inner city, no? JalYt has been past TzHaar-Ket.
Full obsidian make obsidian blade bite harder. JalYt knew that, no?
tzhaar/insult: Obsidian armour on a JalYt. Rock outside, water inside. Still leak.
ogre/compliment: Black shiny rock armour. Hard like ogre's head. Goodly, creature.
ogre/insult: Creature wears a rock. Ogre throws rocks. Dat is where rocks go.
ogre/remark: Dat black glass stuff. Comes from da hot mountain, dey say. Burny.

compliment: Now that's a maul. You could knock down a wall with that.
A great black stone maul. Nobody's going to argue with you.
insult: That maul's bigger than you are. Does it carry you about?
A maul like that, and you still can't open a jar, I bet.
remark: Mind the cobbles with that thing.
guard/insult: That maul stays on your back while you're in town. Understood?
guard/remark: That's a lot of rock on a stick. I'll be watching it.
kid/compliment: Can you smash a house with that?
dwarf/compliment: Obsidian maul, eh? Crude. Honest. I like it.
tzhaar/compliment: Tzhaar-ket-om. Big rock maul. JalYt-Ket, maybe. Strong arms.
Maul of obsidian. TzHaar-Ket carry those. JalYt carry one too. Hm.
tzhaar/remark: Ket-om. Means big club. JalYt name for it is longer. Means same.
tzhaar/insult: Big maul. Slow maul. TzHaar-Xil behind you before it lands.
ogre/compliment: Big rock on a stick! Bestest hitting fing. Creature has good taste.
ogre/insult: Dat maul is bigger dan creature. Ogre would use it as a spoon.
ogre/remark: Creature got a smasher. Smash da rock cakes wiv it. Dey need it.

compliment: Weapons of obsidian. The TzHaar don't hand those out lightly.
insult: A weapon made of glass. Don't drop it.
Obsidian. Lovely and sharp, until you sneeze.
remark: Fire caves gear, that. They say it's warm to the touch.
wizard/remark: Obsidian. The TzHaar's work. Their magic runs rather hot.
kid/remark: Is that made of glass? Can I break it?
dwarf/compliment: Volcanic glass, knapped that clean? Hats off to the TzHaar.
heartland/compliment: Black glass blade. Volcanic, that. Very fierce.
tzhaar/compliment: TokTz blade. TzHaar-Hur made that. JalYt chose well. For a JalYt.
Obsidian in JalYt hand. Hard rock, forged in fire. Like TzHaar.
tzhaar/remark: That blade cost many TokKul at TzHaar-Hur-Tel. Or JalYt was lucky.
tzhaar/insult: Obsidian blade. Good. JalYt arm still soft. Blade can only do so much.
ogre/compliment: Black glass stabber! Sharp sharp. Goodly for da chompies.
ogre/insult: Shiny black knife. Pretty. Creature still weedy behind it. Hur, hur.
ogre/remark: Dat sharp black fing. Me cut a finger on one once. Grrr. Still angry.

compliment: Crystal armour! Like wearing a window. A very hard window.
You're sparkling. Elven work, that, surely.
insult: See-through armour. Does it come with see-through trousers?
Crystal armour. Lovely. Mind the hailstones.
remark: You catch the light something lovely.
kid/compliment: You're all sparkly!
kid/insult: Crystal's for necklaces. My nan said.
wizard/compliment: Elven crystal, sung into shape. Marvellous. Mind the high notes.
dwarf/remark: Crystal armour. Elves sing it, they say. I'd sooner use a hammer.
trader/compliment: Crystal! My friend, that catches the light and my interest.
heartland/remark: Sturdier than it looks, they say. It looks like a wine glass.
gnome/compliment: Crystal armour! Elven work, human. Even gnomes can't sing like that.
gnome/insult: See-through armour, human? Kar, I won't look. Much.
gnome/remark: Crystal from Prifddinas. It's lighter than it looks, they say.
dwarf/compliment: Crystal. No metal in it, but by Guthix, it holds together. Fair.
dwarf/insult: Elf glass. Pretty. I'd still back a rune plate in a scrap.

compliment: A crystal bow! Elven, is it? Beautiful thing.
Glass and light, and it's a weapon. The elves are clever.
insult: A crystal weapon. Very pretty. What happens when it chips?
Lovely crystal. Worth more than the arrows, I expect.
remark: They say that crystal fades if you use it. Like my knees.
kid/compliment: Your bow's made of diamonds!
wizard/remark: Singing crystal. Elven. They won't tell us how it's done. Typical.
rough/remark: Glass bow. Blimey. What's wrong with yew?

compliment: Fremennik gear! You look ready for a northern winter.
Yak hide and horns. Very Rellekka. Very warm.
insult: Dressed for Rellekka. It's not snowing here, you know.
remark: That looks cold just standing there.
Yak hide, is it? Does it still smell of yak?
fremennik/compliment: Hah! You dress like one of us, outerlander. Now fight like one.
Yak hide. You wear it well. The yak would not mind.
fremennik/insult: Our clothes on a southerner. The yak would be ashamed.
kid/compliment: Your hat's got horns! I want horns.
kid/remark: Why have you got horns? Are you a cow?
rough/compliment: Proper northern gear, that. Keeps the wind out.
heartland/insult: Horned helmet. Did you win that, or did a yak lose it?
fremennik/remark: Yrsa sells that. Not to everyone, mind.
moon_clan/compliment: Fremennik hide, and an open mind. Oh my. I did not expect both.
moon_clan/insult: Dressed as a Fremennik. Do try to think less like one, dear.
tortugan/compliment: Fur and hide. A warm shell for a cold sea. Sensible.
tortugan/remark: Yak hide. We do not need it. A shell keeps warm enough.
troll/remark: Fur clothes. Smelly fur-wearing human, like Rellekka ones.
Fur an' horns. Human dress like yak. Troll eat yak too.
troll/insult: Yak hide? Smell like smelly fur town. Human from Rellekka, me bet.
troll/compliment: Yak hide on human. Warm. Trolls not need warm. Trolls got rock skin.
moon_clan_wary/insult: Fremennik hide. Of course. Sent to pick at our secrets.
Dressed as a Fremennik. Thinking like one, too. I can hear it.
That hide smells of Rellekka. So do your thoughts.
Fremennik dress. Do you listen? No. I thought not.
moon_clan_wary/remark: Fremennik gear. We remember what they did. We are not forgetful.
They dress in hides. We dress in thought. You chose.
moon_clan_wary/compliment: Fremennik hide, and a quiet mind in it. I did not know they made any.
barbarian/compliment: Furs and hide! You look like one of us. Nearly.
barbarian/remark: Mountain tribe furs. Our forefathers wore those coming south.
barbarian/insult: Fur and hide, but a city walk. We can tell, you know.

compliment: Armour like a cathedral. You look like you could pass judgement.
White and gold plate. You look like a knight from the old tales.
insult: Judge's armour, that. Who made you the judge?
Dressed like a paladin, and still queuing for bread like us.
vicar/compliment: The Justiciars' plate! Saradomin's old zealots. Wear it humbly.
vicar/remark: Old Saradominist plate. The colours have faded. The zeal, I hope, too.
kid/compliment: You look like a good knight! Not a bad one.
guard/remark: Armour like that, you'll be judging folk. That's my job.
toff/compliment: Justiciar plate. Now that is how one dresses for a sentencing.
heartland/remark: They say the Justiciars never got questioned. I can see why.

compliment: Dark plate, mace to match. You look like a sentence being carried out.
Fearsome kit. I'd confess to anything, me.
insult: You look like you're about to ask me some very pointed questions.
Dressed like an inquisitor, and I've not done anything. Honest.
remark: They say that belonged to a turncloak. Does it still turn?
vicar/remark: The turncloak justiciar's armour. I'll say a prayer for it. And you.
vicar/insult: Inquisitor's plate. I'd ask whose side you're on, but I'm nervous.
kid/insult: You look like a villain. A proper one.
shady/compliment: The turncloak's armour. Now there's a man who saw sense.
guard/remark: Inquisitor, are you? We've no vacancies. Try the dungeons.

compliment: Robes fit for a sorceress of old. Very grand.
Blue and gold robes, trailing magic. Lovely.
insult: Fancy robes. I hope the spells live up to the hems.
Robes like that, and your hems still drag in the mud like ours.
wizard/compliment: Ancestral robes! Those have outlived their first owner, and wisely.
wizard/insult: Robes of a bygone sorceress. On you, they're going through a phase.
kid/compliment: Are you a witch? A good one?
toff/compliment: Robes with some history to them. One approves.
heartland/remark: Those robes have seen some strange rooms, I'd wager.

compliment: Sleek dark armour, trimmed in gold. Desert work, that, surely.
You look fast just standing there. Very sharp.
insult: Ranger armour from the desert. Bit much for the rain, no?
kid/compliment: You look like a shadow with gold on!
trader/compliment: Old desert armour. I'd pay handsomely, and still come out ahead.
toff/remark: Masked, armoured, trimmed in gold. An archer or a very good thief.
heartland/insult: Gold on dark leather. Very fetching. Very noticeable. In a hedge.
heartland/remark: They say the desert rangers wore that. Long gone, they are.

compliment: Dark robes, ancient cut. There's power in those. I can feel it.
Those robes drink the light. Very impressive. Slightly worrying.
insult: Robes that dark, you must get mistaken for a doorway.
Ancient robes. Mysterious. Do they come in a colour?
remark: They say those were dug up with the dead. Looks it, a bit.
wizard/compliment: Virtus robes. Ancient Magicks weave. Handle them with respect.
wizard/remark: Robes from the old empire. The Tower would kill for a thread. Nearly.
vicar/remark: Dark robes, old gods. I shan't pry. I shall pray.
kid/insult: You look like a bat. A posh bat.
shady/compliment: Robes of the old empire. Someone has taste, for once.

compliment: Armour from infernal metal, they say. You wear it well, somehow.
That plate looks forged in a furnace nobody should own. Impressive.
insult: Infernal armour. I hope you read the terms before you put it on.
Armour sworn to something. Hope you remembered what.
remark: That metal glows a bit. Is it meant to glow?
vicar/remark: Infernal metal, worn in daylight. I'll light a candle, just in case.
vicar/insult: Infernal plate. Whatever oath that was, I'd not have sworn it.
guard/remark: Infernal armour inside the walls. I'm writing that down.
kid/insult: You look like you came out of a chimney!
shady/compliment: An oath forged in metal. Now that is commitment.

compliment: Dragon armour! Redder than the Cook's face. Very smart.
That red armour's proper quality. You don't see much of it.
insult: Dragon armour. Very dear. Very red. Very easy to spot in a crowd.
Red metal armour. Hope you didn't have to fight the dragon for it.
plain/insult: Red armour. Lovely. You'll match the blood splatter.
remark: That red metal's rarer than hens' teeth, they say.
They say that's dragon metal. Not from a dragon. Confusing.
kid/compliment: Red armour! Red's the fastest!
dwarf/compliment: Dragon metal. Nobody can smith it, so the story goes. Lovely finish.
dwarf/remark: Dragon metal. I'd give an arm to learn the trick of it. Not mine.
trader/remark: Dragon metal, that. Keep it on. Keeps the price up.
tzhaar/compliment: Red armour. Colour of lava. JalYt chose well, for once.
tzhaar/remark: Red metal armour. No smith can shape it, they say. Lava could.
tzhaar/insult: Red armour. JalYt trying to look like TzHaar. Lava is not fooled.
ogre/compliment: Red shiny armour! Red is da bestest. Red is colour of dinner.
ogre/insult: Dragon armour, creature? Ogre fought a real dragon. Dragon stoopid.
ogre/remark: Red metal. Not from a dragon, dey say. Den why call it dat? Grrr.
gnome/compliment: Red armour, human! You can see you coming from the Grand Tree.
gnome/remark: Dragon metal, they say. No dragons on the glider routes, thank Guthix.
dwarf/insult: Dragon metal. Lovely. And you didn't smith a scrap of it, did you?
fremennik/compliment: Red dragon metal. No smith can work it, they say. Worth a verse.
fremennik/insult: Red armour. Did you fight the dragon, or buy it from a southerner?
moon_clan/compliment: Dragon metal. Red as a good dream. You wear it calmly, dear.
moon_clan/insult: Dragon metal, they say. No dragon in your memories, though. Bought.
tortugan/compliment: Red armour. A gryphon would spot you a mile off. Then think twice.
tortugan/insult: Dragon metal, they say. Not from a dragon. Humans and their names.
goblin/compliment: Red armour! Bentnoze say red best! Thorobshuun tribe colour!
Red armour. Red red red! Me not allowed say that now. Brown now.
goblin/insult: Red armour make you look fat. Wartface say so. He right this once.
Red armour, human? Stupid reddie!
goblin/remark: Red armour best! No, brown. Generals say brown. Red still look nice.
troll/insult: Red metal clothes. Hurt troll teeth. Human cheating.
Red metal armour. No good to eat. Troll chuck dat bit away.
troll/compliment: Red metal! Rare stuff. Human must have eat a dragon to get it.
troll/remark: Red metal. Troll cook pull dat off first. Then stew.
moon_clan_wary/insult: Dragon metal. Bought, by the look of your memories. I had a look.
Dragon metal. Red as a Fremennik temper. You match.
moon_clan_wary/compliment: Dragon metal, worn without swagger. I will give you that much.
guard/remark: Red metal armour. Costs more than the gatehouse. Mind the paint.
guard/insult: Dragon armour in the street. That's a robbery waiting to happen.
guard/compliment: Dragon metal. Whatever you did to afford it, do it outside the walls.
barbarian/compliment: Red metal! Rare. Did you win that in a fight? Say you did.
barbarian/insult: Red armour. Pretty. Does it fight, or just shine?
barbarian/remark: Dragon metal, they call that. We call it a good day's loot.

compliment: That's an axe and a half. You could fell a forest in an afternoon.
A greataxe like that, you've no need to raise your voice.
insult: An axe that size, and you use it for what, kindling?
That axe looks half a ton. No wonder you're out of puff.
remark: Dug that axe out of a barrow, did you? It looks it.
Mind the lintels with that axe.
guard/insult: Axe that size stays on your back in town. One swing, three stalls.
guard/remark: Big axe. I'm noting it. Big note.
kid/compliment: That's the biggest axe I've ever seen!
kid/insult: You can't even lift that. Bet you can't.
rough/compliment: Now that's an axe. Chop a yew in one go, I reckon.
dwarf/remark: Old axe, that. Well kept for something out of a grave.

compliment: A granite maul! Simple, honest, enormous. I like it.
Lump of granite on a stick. Can't go wrong with that.
insult: A rock on a stick. Did it take long to design?
That maul's a bit basic, isn't it? Hits hard, I'm sure. Like a wall.
remark: Granite, that. Heavy as a bad conscience, and about as subtle.
Granite, that. Quarried in the desert, they say.
dwarf/compliment: Granite! Simplicity is the best weapon. Someone understood that.
kid/compliment: It's a hammer made of a mountain!
kid/insult: That's just a rock. My rock's better.
guard/remark: Keep that maul off the paving. We've only just had it relaid.

compliment: A flail! Haven't seen one of those in years. Very proper.
Ball and chain. Old-fashioned, and all the better for it.
insult: Mind that flail. You'll have your own eye out before mine.
A ball on a chain. Do you ever hit yourself with it? Be honest.
remark: A flail. My grandfather had one. For the cattle, he said.
Grave gear, that flail. Smells a bit of crypt.
kid/insult: You're going to hit yourself with that. I'm watching.
kid/compliment: Spin it! Spin it round!
vicar/remark: A flail of the dead, in the churchyard. Let's not wake anyone.
guard/remark: Keep that chain short in the crowds, you.

compliment: A blade with Saradomin's star on it. Very righteous. Very shiny.
A glowing blue blade. Saradomin's own, they say. Lovely.
insult: A holy sword. Hope you've been to church this month, then.
vicar/compliment: Saradomin's own blade! Wield it kindly, traveller. Mostly kindly.
vicar/insult: A holy sword, and I don't recall seeing you at a single service.
shady/insult: Saradomin's toy. Blue and loud, like all his followers.
kid/compliment: Your sword's glowing! Is it magic?
wizard/remark: An Icyene blade. Saradomin's lot do make lovely things, for zealots.
heartland/insult: Saradomin's blade. Does he know you're swinging it at chickens?
heartland/remark: That blade glows. Does it do that in the dark? Handy.

compliment: A godsword! Taller than you. How do you get through doors?
A sword forged in the God Wars, they say. You wear it well.
insult: A sword the size of a door. Do you knock, or just come in?
A godsword. Hope you've a god-sized sheath for it.
sharp/insult: A godsword. The gods must have run out of smaller ones.
remark: That's a lot of sword for market day.
kid/compliment: That sword's bigger than my dad!
kid/insult: Bet you can't even lift it over your head.
vicar/remark: A godsword. I'd ask which god, but I'd rather not start a war.
guard/insult: That sword comes nowhere near the market. I mean it.
guard/remark: Godsword in town. Right. I'm fetching the captain.
dwarf/compliment: A godsword. The hilt alone's a month's work. The blade, a lifetime.
trader/compliment: A godsword, my friend. I'd make you an offer. You'd laugh. Fair.
heartland/remark: They say the gods' own armies fought over those. I believe it.
tzhaar/compliment: Sword of the gods. Taller than JalYt. JalYt carry it anyway. Strong.
tzhaar/remark: Big sword. Good for fight. Bad for narrow tunnels. Mind the walls.
tzhaar/insult: Sword of a god. JalYt did not forge it. Only carry it. Heavy, no?
ogre/compliment: Big sword! Biggest sword! Creature nearly big enough for it.
ogre/insult: Sword bigger dan creature. Yous fall over if yous sneeze. Hur, hur.
ogre/remark: Dat sword could chop a chompy in half. Waste of a chompy.
gnome/compliment: A godsword, human! Longer than I am. Longer than two of me.
gnome/insult: A godsword. Compensating for being so slow, human?
gnome/remark: A sword that size, human? You'd clear the pitch at gnomeball.
dwarf/insult: A godsword, human. Any dwarf would have made the hilt neater.
dwarf/remark: A godsword. Forged in the God Wars, they say. Still sharp, by Guthix.
fremennik/compliment: A sword of the gods. Hang it in the Longhall and we drink to it.
fremennik/insult: A sword that size. Can you lift it, or does it lift you?
moon_clan/compliment: A sword from the God Wars. You carry it without boasting. Rare.
moon_clan/remark: Such a large sword. Oh my. Your thoughts are mostly about doors.
tortugan/compliment: A sword taller than you. Patience, to learn that. I respect patience.
tortugan/insult: A sword that size, at sea, would be an anchor. A fine anchor.
goblin/compliment: Huge sword! From war of gods, they say. Goblins fight in that war!
goblin/insult: Sword bigger than human. Human fall over if human swing it.
goblin/remark: Big sword. Not axe, not hammer. Generals argue about that too.
troll/compliment: Huge sword! Bigger than human. Human carry it good. Troll impressed.
troll/insult: Sword bigger than human. Human fall over if swing it. Troll watch.
troll/remark: Big sword. Troll just use big rock. Rock cheaper.
barbarian/compliment: Now that is a sword! Gunthor would want a swing of that.
barbarian/insult: A sword taller than you. Who carries who?
barbarian/remark: A sword from the god wars, they say. Swing it, don't talk about it.

compliment: A maul like a chunk of mountain. Nobody argues with that.
Now that's a maul. You'd not need to hit anything twice.
insult: Big maul. Is it for fighting, or for propping up the house?
A maul like that, and you knock before entering? Doubt it.
remark: They say that was part of a creature once. Don't tell it.
kid/compliment: Smash something! Go on!
guard/remark: That maul's a public hazard. I'll be behind you. Well behind.
dwarf/remark: Stone maul, that. Not quarried. Grown, they say. Unnatural.

compliment: Crossbow made for dragon hunting, that. You're braver than me.
A dragon-hunting crossbow. Bone and sinew, by the look. Fearsome.
insult: Dragon-hunting crossbow. How many dragons so far? Roughly.
A crossbow for dragons, and you're pointing it at a goblin, I bet.
remark: They say that's made from a dragon's own bones. Rude, if so.
kid/remark: Have you shot a real dragon? What happened?
rough/compliment: Dragon-hunting gear, that. Proper tool for a proper job.
guard/remark: Dragon-hunting crossbow. No dragons in town. Keep it wound down.

compliment: A blowpipe! Very nimble. Very quiet. Very nasty, I expect.
Darts and venom. Clever thing, that.
insult: Is that a flute? Oh. Oh, that's a weapon. Right.
A blowpipe. Do you have to purse your lips at people? How rude.
remark: That pipe's dripping. Is it meant to drip?
Mind where you point that. I've a face I'm fond of.
kid/remark: Is that a flute? Play us a tune!
kid/insult: You spit at people for a living? Mum says that's rude.
barkeep/remark: Keep that blowpipe away from my barrels. One dart and the ale's off.
wizard/insult: A blowpipe. Magic for people who can't do magic.

compliment: A glowing crystal bow. The elves made that, surely. Lovely.
That bow sings when it moves. Did you hear it? I heard it.
insult: Fancy elven bow. Hope your aim's as pretty.
Bow made of light. Hope the arrows aren't.
remark: Elven crystal, that. They don't give those to just anyone. Allegedly.
kid/compliment: Your bow's glowing! Shoot the moon!
wizard/compliment: Crystal of Prifddinas, and sung properly. Now that's craftsmanship.
trader/remark: Elven crystal, my friend. I've nothing in the shop to swap for that.
toff/compliment: Elven work. One approves. One's own bow is merely gilded.

compliment: That shield's the size of a barn door. Nothing's getting past you.
A shield with a face on it. Very fierce. The face, I mean.
insult: Hiding behind a door, are we? A very big door.
Big shield. Is it a shield, or a wall that took a liking to you?
remark: Is that shield looking at me? It is, isn't it.
Mind the stalls with that thing. And the walls. And the people.
kid/insult: You're hiding behind a door!
kid/compliment: Your shield's got a face! Make it talk!
guard/remark: That shield blocks the whole street. Keep to the left. Far left.
dwarf/compliment: Dinh's work. Greatest smith who ever lived, and a dwarf. Naturally.

compliment: A demon-forged defender, they say. Sits nicely on the arm, mind.
insult: Tiny shield. Protecting your elbow, is it?
A shield the size of a dinner plate. Confident, that.
remark: That little shield's got teeth. Mind you don't scratch yourself.
kid/insult: That's a baby shield!
kid/compliment: Your shield's got spikes. I want spikes.
vicar/remark: Demon-made, that defender, they say. I'll sprinkle something on it.
dwarf/compliment: Compact defender, well balanced. Infernal smiths know a thing or two.
heartland/compliment: Little red shield on your arm, spiky as anything. Very smart.

compliment: A rapier! Elegant. You look like you'd fence with manners.
Thin blade, red as wine. Vampyre make, they say. Fearsome.
insult: A rapier. Very elegant. Do you bow before you stab?
A blade that thin, you could lose it in the washing.
remark: They say that came out of Morytania. Red for a reason, I expect.
kid/remark: That's a skinny sword. Is it a toothpick for a giant?
toff/compliment: A rapier. Civilised. One might almost invite you to dinner.
vicar/remark: A blade from the vampyre lands. Blessed, I hope. Twice, ideally.
shady/compliment: A rapier smeared with vampyre blood. Your sort has hidden depths.

compliment: A trident! Handsome thing. Does it come with the weather?
A trident. You look like you've come up out of the sea to sort us out.
insult: A trident. Off fishing, are we? Big fish?
That's for fish, surely. Very big fish. Very angry fish.
remark: A trident. My uncle had one. For the eels.
Does that thing fire water? What a waste of water.
kid/compliment: Are you the king of the sea?!
kid/insult: That's a big fork.
rough/remark: Trident, eh? Catch anything? No? Thought not.
wizard/insult: A trident that does the casting for you. Spells for the lazy.
pirate/compliment: Arr, a trident! Ye've been talking to the deep, have ye?

compliment: A staff crowned with red. Vampyre make, and powerful, they say.
That staff pulses. Like a heart. Impressive. Unsettling. Impressive.
insult: A staff that drinks blood, they say. Does it share?
Red staff. Hope that's paint. It's not paint, is it.
remark: A staff from the vampyre lands, they say. Rather you than me.
vicar/remark: Blood magic in a stick. I'll stand over here, if it's all the same.
wizard/compliment: Blood magic, bound in a staff. Dreadful. Brilliant. Mostly dreadful.
kid/insult: Your stick's bleeding.
shady/compliment: A blood staff. Your sort's finally learning.

compliment: A twisted dark staff with a glowing orb. You've been somewhere awful.
That staff looks like a bad dream carved in wood. In a good way.
insult: That staff gives me the shivers. Do you sleep with it?
An orb on a stick. Very mystical. Does it do party tricks?
remark: They say that came off a nightmare. An actual one. Over in Slepe.
I'll not sleep tonight, looking at that staff.
wizard/compliment: An orb like that on a staff. The Tower would weep. With envy.
wizard/remark: Harmonised orb? Volatile? Don't tell me. I'd like to keep my eyebrows.
kid/insult: Your stick's giving me nightmares. Mum!
vicar/remark: A nightmare on a staff. I shall pray for whoever dreamt it.
nan/remark: Ooh, I don't like that staff, dear. Put it away before bedtime.

compliment: A mime! Lovely. Go on, do the wall. Everyone loves the wall.
Black and white stripes. Very dramatic. Very quiet, I hope.
insult: A mime. Finally, an adventurer who'll keep quiet.
Dressed as a mime. Say something. No? Oh, very good.
remark: You're not stuck in an invisible box, are you? Blink twice.
kid/compliment: Do the invisible rope! Do it!
kid/insult: Mimes are creepy. My sister said.
barkeep/remark: A mime. Good. Last one in here never shut up.
toff/insult: A mime. At last, a performer one can ignore in silence.

compliment: Love the zombie look. You've really let yourself go. Convincingly.
Dressed as the walking dead! You shamble beautifully.
insult: Are you dressed as a zombie, or is that just how it's going?
Zombie outfit. Suits you. Not sure that's a compliment.
remark: You smell a bit of grave. Is that part of the costume?
Shambling about town, dressed like that. Very Morytania.
kid/compliment: A zombie! Do the walk! Do the walk!
kid/insult: You're not a real zombie. Real ones smell worse.
vicar/remark: Dressed as the undead, outside my church. Subtle. Very subtle.
vicar/insult: The dead rise, and they're wearing that. I'll fetch the holy water.
nan/remark: Ooh, you look dreadful, dear. Oh, it's on purpose. Still.

compliment: A severed head. Very dramatic. Was he a friend?
insult: Is that head yours, or did you find it?
You're holding a head. Just so you know. In case you hadn't noticed.
remark: Is that head talking to you? It looks like it wants to.
Put that head away. The children. Well, the chickens.
kid/compliment: A head! Can I hold it? Can it talk?
kid/insult: Mum! That one's got a head!
vicar/remark: A head. Carried by hand. He'd have liked a burial, I expect.
guard/remark: That head. Where did you get that head? No. Don't tell me.
shady/remark: Carrying a head about. I can respect a statement.
heartland/compliment: Carrying a head about. Bold. Is it anyone we know?

compliment: A hat with a feather. Shorts in this weather. I admire the commitment.
remark: Are those shorts leather? Do they squeak when you walk?
Off up a mountain, are we? Or just dressed for one?
kid/compliment: I like your shorts! They look like a drum!
kid/insult: Why are you in shorts? Are you a baby?
dwarf/compliment: Mountain clothes! Now you're dressed for proper country. Beer?
toff/insult: Leather shorts. One assumes the trousers were stolen.
heartland/compliment: Leather shorts and long socks! Ready for a hike, I see.
heartland/insult: Leather shorts. In this weather. Your knees must be furious.
A hat with goat hair on it. Did the goat agree to that?

compliment: Camouflage! Very clever. I nearly walked into you.
Blending in with the hedges. Clever. Hedges are very underrated.
remark: Who said that? I can't see anyone. Oh. There you are.
You look like a bush that's learnt to walk.
kid/compliment: I can't see you! Where'd you go? Where'd you go?
kid/insult: I can see you. You're rubbish at hiding.
guard/remark: Camouflage inside the walls. Suspicious. Also ineffective.
rough/remark: Dressed like a hedge. Blimey. Poachers these days.
heartland/insult: Camouflage, and I can see you perfectly well. Try a bigger hedge.
Hiding in plain sight, are we? Plain sight can see you, you know.

compliment: Royal robes, in frog green. Kissed anyone lately? Anyone croak?
Dressed like a prince out of a story. The frog kind. Lovely.
insult: Royal dress, and not a single footman. Standards have slipped.
Royalty, is it? The frog kind, by the look of it.
remark: Is that frog royalty you're dressed as? There's a story there.
Posh, and a bit swampy. I'll not ask.
kid/compliment: Are you a prince? Are you a frog? Are you both?
kid/insult: You look like a frog in a dress.
toff/insult: Royal dress. Frog royalty, admittedly. Still, a step up.
toff/compliment: Royal attire! A frog's court, granted, but one takes what one can.
nan/remark: Ooh, very posh, dear. Did a frog kiss you? They do that.

compliment: A shirt with Bob on it! The cat from Burthorpe. Good taste.
Bob's shirt! He gives such sensible advice, that cat.
insult: A shirt with a cat on it. Does the cat know?
A cat shirt. Bob's got better things to do than be on your front.
remark: That cat on your shirt looks like he wants a word.
Bob says something or other, I expect. Bob always does.
kid/compliment: It's Bob! I love Bob! Can I stroke your shirt?
kid/insult: Bob's shirt's better on Bob.
nan/compliment: Ooh, Bob! Lovely cat, that. Always says to mind your purse.
banker/remark: Bob says keep your valuables in the bank. Bob is quite right.
trader/remark: Bob says mind your coins. Bad for business, that cat.

compliment: Father Christmas himself! Have you brought the presents?
The whole Santa suit! Very jolly. Mind the chimneys.
insult: Father Christmas, is it? You've lost weight. And the sleigh.
Santa suit. Bit early. Or very, very late.
remark: Evening, Santa. I was good this year. Mostly.
Red suit, white trim, no sleigh. The reindeer have more sense.
kid/compliment: Santa! I've been good! Ask my mum! Don't ask my mum.
kid/insult: You're not the real Santa. The real one's fatter.
nan/remark: Father Christmas, dear? You've not eaten enough. Have a biscuit.
barkeep/remark: Santa! Sherry's on the house. Well, it's on the bar. Pay for it.

compliment: A Santa hat in the wrong colours. I've heard of those. Never seen one.
That hat's worth more than my house. And my neighbour's.
insult: A Santa hat gone wrong. Did it come out of the wash like that?
Christmas hat, wrong colour. Even Santa makes mistakes, I suppose.
remark: Mind that hat round here. It'd buy half the town.
They say Santa had a wicked twin. Is that his hat?
kid/compliment: Your Santa hat's the wrong colour! That's brilliant.
kid/insult: Santa's hat is red. Yours is wrong. You're wrong.
trader/compliment: That hat, my friend. Name a figure. I'll sell the shop.
shady/remark: A hat like that walks home alone, does it? Interesting.
banker/remark: A hat of that value ought to be in a vault, not on a head.

compliment: A Christmas jumper! Very cosy. Did your nan knit that?
Festive jumper. Lovely. I can almost smell the mince pies.
insult: A Christmas jumper. Did you lose a bet, or win one?
Festive jumper. It's not even snowing. Commitment, I'll give you that.
kid/compliment: I like your jumper! It's all woolly!
kid/insult: My nan made me one like that. I hid it.
nan/compliment: Ooh, a jumper like that takes weeks. Somebody loves you, dear.
barkeep/remark: Christmas jumper. Mulled wine's not on till the frost, mind.
heartland/remark: A Christmas jumper. Now I feel I ought to have got you something.

compliment: Bunny feet! Lucky, those. Not for the rabbit, mind.
A rabbit costume. You hop beautifully. Carry on.
insult: Dressed as a rabbit. Have you been at the carrots?
Big furry feet. Do you leave footprints the size of plates?
remark: Rabbit ears and big feet. The eggs will be along shortly, I expect.
Those feet look warm. I'll say that for them.
kid/compliment: A bunny! Hop! Hop for me!
kid/insult: You're a rubbish rabbit. Real ones are smaller.
rough/remark: Big rabbit. Blimey. Keep it off my lettuces.
nan/remark: Ooh, bunny feet. Your mother dress you, did she, dear?

compliment: Egg helmet! Cracking, that is.
insult: An egg on your head. Did a very large hen have a go at you?
Egg head. Literally. I'd not stand near a frying pan.
remark: Mind you don't crack that. Your head, I mean. Well, both.
kid/compliment: Egg head! Is there chocolate in it? Is there?
kid/insult: Egg head! Egg head! Egg head!
barkeep/remark: Egg on your head. Don't tempt the cook.
nan/remark: An egg, dear? On your head? Well, it's better than in your hair.
heartland/compliment: An egg for a head! Very festive. Don't let the hens see.

compliment: Easter gear! Lovely. Where've you hidden the eggs?
Happy Easter, traveller. Chocolate for breakfast, I hope.
insult: Easter get-up. Did the bunny dress you, or was it a dare?
An Easter outfit. The chickens must be very confused.
kid/compliment: Easter! Have you got eggs? Give me the eggs!
kid/insult: Where's my egg? You've got no eggs. Rubbish.
vicar/remark: Easter finery! Do come to the service. Bring an egg for the plate.
heartland/remark: Is it Easter? The eggs in the coop have gone very quiet.

compliment: Pale robes, half there. Very haunting. Lovely.
insult: You're looking a bit transparent. Have you eaten?
Ghost robes. Are you dead, or just dressed for it?
remark: Can I see through you, or is that the robes?
You gave me a turn. Thought you were a ghost. Are you a ghost?
kid/compliment: A ghost! Say woooo! Say it!
kid/insult: You're not a real ghost. I poked you.
vicar/remark: Those robes. I nearly reached for the holy water. I may still.
vicar/insult: Ghostly robes. If you're here for the exorcism, you're early.
nan/remark: You look half dead, dear. Oh, it's the robes. Still, eat something.
barkeep/remark: Thought you were the pub ghost for a second. He owes me money.
heartland/compliment: Ghostly robes! You look very... elsewhere. It suits you.

compliment: A pumpkin for a head! Cheered me right up, that. Mind the crows.
Pumpkin head! You've made my Halloween, that has.
insult: A pumpkin on your head. Is that a mask, or did one grow there?
Pumpkin head. Don't light a candle in it. Or do. I'd watch.
remark: Pumpkin for a head. Hollowed it out yourself, did you?
Mind the candles with that head.
kid/compliment: Pumpkin head! Can I carve a face in it? Oh, there is one.
kid/insult: You've got a vegetable for a head. A vegetable.
nan/remark: Pumpkin on your head, dear? That'd have made a lovely pie.
barkeep/remark: Pumpkin head. Soup's off, then.

compliment: A skeleton! Very spooky. All your bones on the outside. Tidy.
Dressed as a skeleton. You've a lovely set of bones, I must say.
insult: A skeleton. Have you eaten? Ever?
Dressed as bones. I've seen more meat on a butcher's pencil.
remark: Bones on the outside. Saves the undertaker a job.
kid/compliment: A skeleton! Rattle for me!
kid/insult: You're not scary. The ones in the sewers are scarier.
vicar/insult: Dressed as the dead, by the graveyard. The tenants won't be amused.
nan/remark: Skin and bone, dear. Literally. Come in and have some stew.

compliment: Dressed as Death himself! Very convincing. I've gone cold.
The reaper's robes. Marvellous. You've ruined my afternoon.
insult: Dressed as Death. Have you come for me, or just for the bread?
The Grim Reaper, in the daytime. Bit keen, aren't you?
remark: Is it my time? It's not my time. Is it?
kid/compliment: It's death! Hi, Death!
kid/insult: You're not real Death. Real Death has a scythe.
vicar/remark: Death, outside my church. You're early. Nobody's booked.
nan/remark: Ooh, Death, is it? Not today, dear. I've a cake in the oven.
barkeep/remark: Death's in. Drinks on him, I should hope.
heartland/remark: If you're Death, I'd like a word about my knees.

compliment: Goggles and a scarf. You look like you've been up and liked it.
Ooh, a gnome scarf. Tally ho! Off up in a glider, are we?
insult: A gnome's scarf. Did you borrow it off a very small pilot?
Goggles on your head. Expecting weather, or just being dramatic?
remark: A scarf like that, you'll be joining the glider pilots next.
gnome/compliment: A gnome scarf, human! You've eaten well with us, I see.
gnome/remark: Dressed like a pilot, human. The gliders will think you're one.
kid/compliment: Goggles! Are you a pilot? Take me up!
kid/insult: You've got a gnome's scarf. Did you steal it off a gnome?

compliment: A clown! Marvellous. Do the thing with the shoes.
Big shoes, stripy trousers. You've cheered the whole street up.
insult: Dressed as a clown. Was that the plan, or did it just happen?
Clown outfit. Very brave. Half the town's scared of clowns.
plain/insult: A clown. Finally, a job you look qualified for.
remark: Those shoes. How do you climb stairs?
Is there a circus in town, or is it just you?
kid/compliment: A clown! Do a trick! Fall over!
kid/insult: I don't like clowns. Go away. No, come back. Go away.
nan/remark: Ooh, a clown, dear. I've never trusted them. Biscuit?
toff/insult: A clown. The court jester's position is filled, citizen. Ably.

compliment: Dressed as a cow! Udderly brilliant.
A cow costume. Very convincing. The farmers'll be after you.
remark: Mind the farmer doesn't try to milk you.
kid/compliment: A cow! Moo! Say moo! Say it!
kid/insult: You're not a real cow. Real ones don't walk on two legs.
rough/remark: Cow, is it? Fine. Into the field with the others.
rough/insult: Dressed as a cow. I've a bull who'd like a word.
barkeep/remark: A cow. It's steak night. Best not look at the specials board.
heartland/insult: Dressed as a cow. Are you going to the field, or from it?
A cow. Right. Moo, I suppose.
heartland/remark: I was going to say something, but a cow walked past. You, I mean.

compliment: Dressed as a chicken! Very brave. The foxes will love you.
A chicken costume. Lovely plumage. Does it moult?
insult: Dressed as a chicken. What's the matter? Are you?
A chicken outfit. Mind the cook. He's got a cleaver.
remark: A chicken. In town. Cluck once if you're all right.
kid/compliment: A chicken! Flap! Flap your wings!
kid/insult: Chickens can't even fly. Neither can you.
barkeep/remark: A chicken. Kitchen's that way, if you're volunteering.
rough/remark: Chicken, eh? Mind the fox. He's had three this week.
heartland/remark: The chickens in Lumbridge are going to be very confused.

compliment: A powdered wig! Very distinguished. Very judge.
That wig takes years off you. Or adds a title. One or the other.
insult: A powdered wig. Are you a judge, or did a sheep land on you?
Lovely wig. Big do about nothing, if you ask me.
remark: Is that wig powdered, or has a baker sneezed on you?
A wig like that, you'll be sentencing people by teatime.
kid/compliment: Your hair's huge! Is it real? Can I pull it?
kid/insult: You look like an old lady. A fancy one.
toff/compliment: A powdered wig. Now that is how one dresses to be obeyed.
toff/insult: A powdered wig on a commoner. The sheep must be furious.
banker/remark: A wig like that, I feel I should call you 'your honour'.

compliment: A highwayman's mask! Very dashing. Stand and deliver, I suppose.
Masked like a highwayman. You've a flair for it.
insult: A highwayman mask. Your money or your life? I've neither, so.
Masked up. Robbing anyone today, or just dressed for it?
remark: Mind the guards see that mask. They'll have questions.
Masked, in daylight. Bold.
kid/compliment: A robber! Rob me! I've got a button!
kid/insult: You're not a real robber. A real one would've robbed me.
guard/insult: Highwayman mask. Take it off, or come with me. Your choice.
guard/remark: A mask. In town. I'm writing this down. Slowly.
trader/remark: A highwayman's mask, my friend? Stand well away from the till.
shady/compliment: A mask with purpose. Now you're dressing properly.

item.pattern: ^(Pirate('s)? (hat|hook|bandana|boots|leggings)|Stripy pirate|Big pirate hat|(Right|Left) eye patch|Hat eyepatch)
item.label: pirate gear

compliment: You've a proper sea dog look about you. Arr, as they say.
insult: Dressed as a pirate. Nearest sea's miles off, you know.
remark: Pirates in town. Lock up the rum.
You've the hat. Have you the ship? No? Just the hat, then.
pirate/compliment: Arr! A proper buccaneer! Ye'll do, matey.
pirate/insult: Arr, pirate clothes on a landlubber. Ye've never seen a wave.
kid/compliment: A pirate! Where's your treasure? Is it buried? Where?
kid/insult: You're not a pirate. You haven't even got a hook. Oh. Still.
barkeep/remark: Pirate, is it? Rum's that way. Pay up front.
banker/remark: Pirate dress. I'll be keeping my hand on the drawer.
heartland/compliment: Pirate gear! Very salty. Where's the parrot?
heartland/insult: A pirate, are you? Lost the ship in a card game, I expect.
parrot/insult: Squawk! Just the hat! Just the hat!
mos_pirate/remark: Arr, one of us, be ye? Or just dressed as one?
mos_pirate/compliment: Now that be proper pirate rig, and no mistake.
mos_pirate/insult: Just the hat, is it? Where's yer ship, landlubber?

compliment: A pith helmet! Off exploring, are we? Very intrepid.
Explorer's hat. You look like you'd know where north is.
insult: An explorer's hat, and you're lost in the market.
remark: Off to the jungle, are we? Mind the snakes.
Explorer, are you? Explore the queue like the rest of us.
kid/compliment: Are you an explorer? Have you found a dinosaur?
kid/insult: Explorers find things. You've found a hat.
toff/compliment: A pith helmet. Splendid. One does like an explorer. From a distance.
trader/remark: An explorer! I've maps, my friend. Mostly accurate.
heartland/insult: Pith helmet. Discovered anything, or just the bakery?

compliment: Bucket helm! Honest ironmongery. Nobody's getting through that.
insult: You've a bucket on your head. Did you know? You do now.
A bucket helmet. Did the well run dry, or did you?
plain/insult: Bucket on your head. Hope you emptied it first.
remark: Is that a bucket? It's a bucket.
Does it echo in there? Say something.
kid/insult: You've got a bucket on your head! Ha ha ha! A bucket!
kid/compliment: Nice bucket. Can I have a go?
dwarf/remark: A bucket helm. Well, it's iron. And it's on your head. It counts.
rough/remark: Hang on. That's where me bucket went.
toff/insult: A bucket. On a head. The peasantry innovates.
banker/remark: A bucket helm. We don't judge here. We simply note.
heartland/compliment: A bucket for a helmet. Resourceful. I respect that.

compliment: HAM robes! Very pink. Humans Against Monsters, is it? Brave.
Dressed as a HAM member. Convincing. Mind the actual ones.
insult: HAM robes. Pink suits you. The cause doesn't.
Humans Against Monsters, eh? You look more Humans Against Laundry.
remark: They call that crimson. It's pink. Everyone knows it's pink.
Off to the HAM hideout, are you? Say hello to the sergeant.
kid/insult: You're pink! Pink pink pink!
kid/remark: Are you in the HAM? Mum says they're all daft.
vicar/remark: HAM robes. Zeal without sense. I'd stick to the pink, if I were you.
shady/insult: HAM. Pink-robed fools shouting at goblins. Your sort fits right in.
guard/remark: HAM robes. We know your lot. Behave.
dwarf/insult: Humans Against Monsters. And dwarves count as what, exactly?
gnome/insult: HAM robes, human? You know what they think of my people. Hmph.

compliment: Desert robes. Sensible, those. The sun's got no purchase on you.
You look cool as a cucumber in those.
insult: Desert robes. It's drizzling. Is it drizzling where you're from?
remark: Those robes'll be no good when the wind gets up.
kid/remark: Why are you in your nightie?
kid/insult: You look like you've been in the bath. A sandy bath.
nan/remark: Desert robes, dear? You'll catch your death up here. Put a coat on.
trader/compliment: Desert cloth! Fine weave. Al Kharid prices, I expect.
heartland/insult: Dressed for Al Kharid. We've got cloud here. Lots of it.
heartland/remark: Back from the desert, are you? Any sand in your boots still?
camel/remark: Desert robes. Sensible. You'll still burn, but slower.
camel/compliment: Dressed for the sand at last. Most of you arrive in iron.
camel/insult: Robes for the heat. The desert will not be impressed. Nor am I.

compliment: Mole slippers! Lovely. Comfiest feet in the kingdom, those.
Slippers shaped like moles. Fond of them, me. Marvellous.
insult: Slippers. Outdoors. In public. Dear me.
Slippers shaped like moles. Did you lose the real shoes down a hole?
remark: Mole slippers. Popped out for the milk and kept going, did you?
kid/compliment: Your shoes have faces! Little mole faces!
kid/insult: You're in your slippers. Outside. You're in trouble.
nan/compliment: Ooh, slippers. Sensible. Nobody wears slippers any more.
rough/remark: Mole slippers. Had one in me field for a month. Not the slipper.
heartland/remark: Those slippers'll be ruined in the mud.

compliment: A gnome child's hat! Adorable. Does it come in grown-up?
Little hat. Big head. Somehow it works.
insult: Is that a gnome child's hat? Did you take it off a gnome child?
Lovely hat. Was the gnome child done with it?
remark: Your hat's a bit small. Or your head's a bit big. One of the two.
gnome/remark: A gnome child's hat, human? Our children are wondering where it went.
gnome/compliment: Dressed like one of our little ones, human. How sweet.
kid/compliment: Nice hat! Swap you for my hat? Mine's got a hole.
kid/insult: That's a baby hat. You've got a baby hat on.
nan/compliment: Ooh, what a dear little hat. Did you make it yourself?

compliment: A sled! Well, it's a bold choice for a weapon, I'll give you that.
Carrying a sled about. Hopeful. I like hopeful.
remark: Off up the mountain with that, are you? Mind the trolls.
kid/compliment: A sled! Give me a go! Where's the snow? Find some!
kid/insult: No snow. You're just carrying a plank. A fancy plank.
trader/remark: A sled, my friend? I've snow out the back. Well, a bucket of ice.
fremennik/compliment: Hah! A sled! Now you're thinking like a northerner, outerlander.
rough/remark: Blimey. Haven't seen a sled since the big snow.
heartland/insult: A sled. In this weather. Was there a mix-up at the stables?
A sled. Where's the snow? Where's the hill? Where's the sense?
heartland/remark: There's no snow here. Was there snow where you started?

compliment: A cloak that drinks the shadows. Ardougne work, that.
That cloak's done some good deeds round Ardougne, by the look.
insult: Shadowy cloak. Planning on sneaking anywhere, or just dressed for it?
A cloak like that says 'Ardougne'. So does the pickpocketing.
remark: Ardougne cloak. Mind the market there. Lot of light fingers.
kid/remark: Are you a spy? You look like a spy.
guard/remark: Ardougne cloak. Their guards have stories about those. Behave.
shady/compliment: A cloak for the shadows. Sensible.

compliment: That cape! You've done every good deed in every town, they say.
A cape covered in badges. You've been everywhere, haven't you.
insult: A cape for being helpful everywhere. Must be exhausting. For us.
Done every errand in the kingdom, and still no sit-down. Shame.
remark: You've helped out in every town, by the look of that. Even Yanille.
kid/compliment: Have you been everywhere? Have you been to the moon?
kid/insult: A cape for doing chores. My mum would love you.
toff/compliment: Service to every province. One ought to knight you. One won't.
banker/remark: A cape for diligence. We admire diligence here. Quietly.

compliment: A cape with notes on it! Heard every tune in the land, have you?
A music cape! Very cultured. Hum us something.
insult: A cape for listening to music. Hard work, was it?
Music cape. Do you take requests? No? Pity.
remark: Is that cape humming, or is it you?
Every song in Gielinor, they say. Even the Party Room one.
kid/compliment: Sing something! Sing!
kid/insult: Music's boring. Have you got a sword instead?
barkeep/remark: Music cape. We've a lute behind the bar. Nobody's brave enough.
toff/compliment: A patron of the arts! One is almost impressed, citizen.

compliment: Saradomin's colours on your back. Very proper.
A blue cape with the star. Saradomin smile on you.
insult: Saradomin's colours. Does he know you're wearing them?
remark: Saradomin's cape, from the mage arena, they say. Brave place to shop.
vicar/compliment: Saradomin's cape! A fellow of the faith. Do come in.
vicar/insult: Saradomin's colours, and I still don't see you Sundays.
shady/insult: Saradomin's cape. He does like his people to be seen. Pity.
kid/remark: Is that the good god or the bad god?
wizard/remark: Saradomin's cape. From Kolodion's arena, I expect. He owes me a drink.
heartland/insult: Saradomin's cape. Been to church lately, or just the Wilderness?

compliment: Zamorak's colours! Bold. Chaos has its charms, I'm told.
Red cape, Zamorak's mark. You've picked a side, and it's a lively one.
insult: Zamorak's cape. Chaos, is it? Your outfit certainly agrees.
remark: Zamorak's colours. Keep that quiet in Falador.
vicar/insult: Zamorak's cape. Outside my church. I'll pray for you. Loudly.
vicar/remark: Zamorak's colours. The door's open to all. Wipe your feet twice.
shady/compliment: Zamorak's colours. Finally, someone with sense.
kid/insult: That's the bad god's cape! The vicar's going to go spare.
guard/remark: Zamorak's cape. The watch has no view on it. Officially.
heartland/insult: Zamorak's cape. Hope you've a good excuse for the vicar.

compliment: Guthix's green. Balance in all things. Very sensible.
A Guthix cape. The druids would approve.
insult: Guthix's cape. Balanced, are you? You're leaning a bit.
Green cape for the god of balance. Still can't walk straight, I see.
remark: Guthix's colours. Sitting on the fence, nicely dressed.
vicar/remark: Guthix's cape. Neither here nor there. Rather like my sermons.
kid/remark: Green cape! Are you a druid? Can you do the rain thing?
shady/insult: Guthix. The god of not deciding. Suits you.

compliment: That contraption on your back. Is that a chicken? Clever.
They say a lady in Draynor Manor builds those. Clever woman.
insult: There's a chicken on your back. Did you know? It knows.
A bag with a chicken in it. Is that armour, or lunch?
remark: Your cape's clucking.
Mind that magnet near the cutlery.
kid/compliment: There's a chicken on your back! Can I feed it?
kid/insult: Your chicken looks sad. You're a bad chicken owner.
rough/remark: One o' my hens went missing last week. That it?
wizard/remark: A magnetic chicken. Not magic, strictly. Still, one admires the nerve.
trader/remark: Device on your back, is it? I sell arrows. You'll be wanting fewer.

insult: A wooden shield. Lovely for kindling, if it comes to that.
plain/insult: A practice sword. The goblins are ever so worried.
kid/insult: Your shield's made of wood! So's my door.
heartland/compliment: Fresh from the combat tutor? Well, everyone starts somewhere.

compliment: Leather. Sensible. It won't rust in the rain, at least.
insult: Leather armour. It'll keep the drizzle off, if not the goblins.
rough/remark: Lumbridge cowhide, that. I'd know those cows anywhere.
kid/remark: You smell like a cow. A nice cow, though.
guard/compliment: Leather. Nothing a watchman need worry about. Carry on.
guard/remark: Leather armour. Same as ours, only yours fits.
guard/insult: Leather. Not armour, strictly. A thick coat with ambitions.

compliment: Studs on the leather. Coming up in the world, aren't you?
insult: All those studs. Do they do anything, or are they for show?
dwarf/remark: Studs knocked into hide. Rough work, but somebody tried.
kid/compliment: Your armour's got buttons all over! Can I press one?
guard/remark: Studded leather. Studs are for show. The watch has tried.
guard/insult: Studs on the leather. Don't lean on the paintwork.
guard/compliment: Studded leather. Sensible. Nobody starts a riot in studded leather.

compliment: Iron armour. Up from bronze, then? Good for you.
insult: Iron armour. Give it a wipe, it's going orange at the edges.
dwarf/insult: Iron. We use that for horseshoes, human.
kid/insult: Your armour's gone rusty! Did you leave it out in the rain?
gnome/compliment: Iron, human. Sturdy. Just don't fall in the river.
gnome/insult: Iron armour, and you still want a lift on a glider? Kar.
dwarf/compliment: Iron. Plain, honest and worked by hand. I'll not sneer.
dwarf/remark: Iron rusts, human. Keep it oiled or it'll go orange on you.
goblin/insult: Grey armour. Grey not a goblin colour. Grey not even a colour.
goblin/remark: Iron. Generals want big lump of iron for soldiers. For hitting.
goblin/compliment: Iron armour. Strong goblin swing big lump of iron. Human just wear it.
troll/insult: Iron on human. Still tinned human. Just harder tin.
troll/remark: Iron armour. Trolls not bother. Trolls got rock skin for free.
troll/compliment: Iron. Heavy. Human carry heavy good. Nearly troll.
guard/remark: Iron. Same as the cell doors. You'll feel at home if it comes to it.
guard/insult: Iron armour, and rusting. Keep it off the benches.
guard/compliment: Iron. Honest metal. Nothing to worry a watchman.
barbarian/remark: Iron. Good honest metal. Half the longhall wears it.
barbarian/insult: Iron plate, dented already? Or did it come that way?
barbarian/compliment: Iron on your back. Plain and heavy. That's how we like it.

compliment: Steel armour. Nice and bright. Someone's been saving up.
insult: Steel. Everyone's got steel. You'll blend right in.
rough/compliment: Good steel, that. Somebody had a long day at the furnace.
kid/compliment: You're all shiny! I can see my face in you!
gnome/compliment: Steel! Bright as a glider wing, human. Smart.
gnome/remark: Steel armour. Humans do love clanking about.
dwarf/compliment: Steel. Now we're talking. Who hammered that out?
dwarf/insult: Steel's fine. My apprentice makes steel. On a slow day.
dwarf/remark: Steel. Twice the coal, twice the strength. Worth it, human.
goblin/insult: Shiny grey armour. Shiny grey still grey. Human pick proper colour.
goblin/remark: Steel armour. All humans wear that. Humans all look same anyway.
goblin/compliment: Steel look strong. Not brown, but strong. Me allow it.
troll/insult: Steel. Shiny tin. Hurt troll teeth, so trolls just squish it flat.
troll/remark: Steel human. Clang clang when walk. Trolls hear you coming from far.
troll/compliment: Shiny steel. Human look like strong tin. Strong tin good.
guard/remark: Steel. Half the town's in steel. Hard to tell you apart. Useful.
guard/insult: Steel armour. Fancy yourself a guard? We've standards. Low ones.
guard/compliment: Steel. Decent kit. Keep it clean and I've no complaints.
barbarian/remark: Steel. Every city soldier wears it. You could pass for one.
barbarian/insult: Shiny steel. Not a scratch on it. So you've not used it.
barbarian/compliment: Steel, and scratched. Now that's armour that's been somewhere.

compliment: Black armour. Very striking. Very serious.
insult: All in black. You're not one of the Black Knights, I hope?
remark: The White Knights won't like that colour on you.
kid/remark: Are you a Black Knight? My mum says they're wicked.
goblin/remark: Black armour. Huzamogaarb tribe wear black. Human from that tribe?
goblin/insult: Black armour make human look like shadow. Ugly shadow.
goblin/compliment: Black armour. Dark colour. Goblins like dark earthy colour. Close.
guard/remark: Black armour. Stands out at night. Makes my job easier.
Black armour. Not against the rules. I did check.
guard/insult: Black armour. I'll need to see what's under the helmet.

compliment: A curved sword. Bought in Al Kharid, I expect. Very dashing.
plain/insult: Did that sword come curved, or did you sit on it?
guard/remark: Keep that blade put away in town. I'm watching.
kid/compliment: Your sword's all bendy! Is it a pirate sword?

compliment: A staff with a little orb on top. Very proper.
insult: Lovely staff. Do you walk with it as well, or is it for show?
